passages.original: Vero dico, quia illi ipsi, quibus cum periculosa et falsa misericordia indulgere videmur, cum ante tribunal Christi pro tantis peccatis damnandi advenerint, contra nos ipsas causas dicturi sunt, dicentes : quod dum aut asperitatem linguæ eorum expavimus, aut falsa blandimenta et pcriculosas adulationes ipsorum libenter accepimus, nos eos dum illis inutilitatem indulgemus in peccatis permanere, aut ipsa peccata etiam augere permiserimus : nec recordantes illud quod in Veteri Testamento scriptum est : Quia per unum peccantem contra omnes ira Dei desaeviit. 0 pietas! 0 misericordia! Uni parcere, et omnes per exemplum malum in discrimen adducere! Non ita suadet sanctus et beatissimus Cyprianus martyr dicens : Qui peccantem verbis adulantibus alat peccandi fomitem subministrat. Nec perimit delicta illi, sed fovet iterum, imperitus medicus, qui tumentes vulnerum sinus manu parcente contrectat; et ab<conditum in profundis secessibus virus, dum servat, exaggerat. Unde et sanctus Joannes Constantinopolitanus episcopus arguit dicens : Imperitus medicus est qui indigesta putredine superducit vulneri cicatriccm.
passages.english: I speak the truth: those very people whom we seem to indulge with a dangerous and false mercy, when they come before the tribunal of Christ to be condemned for such great sins, will plead these very charges against us, saying that, while we either dreaded the harshness of their tongue or gladly accepted their false flatteries and dangerous adulation, we, by indulging their worthlessness, allowed them to remain in their sins or even to increase those sins; nor did we remember what is written in the Old Testament: that through one man's sinning the wrath of God raged against all. O piety! O mercy! To spare one, and to bring all into danger through a bad example! Not so does the holy and most blessed martyr Cyprian advise, saying: "He who nourishes a sinner with flattering words supplies the tinder for sinning. Nor does he destroy his offences, but rather fosters them again, the unskilled physician who handles the swollen cavities of wounds with a sparing hand, and, while he keeps in the poison hidden in the deep recesses, makes it worse." Hence also holy John, bishop of Constantinople, rebukes [this], saying: "He is an unskilled physician who draws a scar over a wound while the putrefaction is not yet drained."
passages.notes: "inutilitatem indulgemus" is odd; perhaps corrupt for "in utilitatem" or similar; rendered literally as "indulging their worthlessness". Scanning errors corrected (pcriculosas, ab<conditum, cicatriccm). The Old Testament allusion is probably to Achan (Joshua 7; cf. Joshua 22:20).
